newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal drops on earnings quality concerns.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal drops on earnings quality concerns.

text.p: Shares of AlliedSignal Inc dropped about 4.4 percent after investors were disappointed by first quarter weakness in the company's chemicals and automotive units, analysts said.
AlliedSignal, a component of the Dow industrials, dropped 3-1/4 to 70-1/2 in afternoon trading.

"There was some concern about the quality of the earnings. The chemical business was weak and automotive was soft. Aerospace really carried the quarter," said George Shapiro, an analyst with Salomon Brothers.
Allied Signal told analysts it did not expect the weakness in chemicals and automotive to linger past the first quarter, analysts said.

AlliedSignal's uneven strength in the first quarter "wasn't a surprise to those who follow the company closely, but it may have been of some concern," said Jeffrey Sprague, an analyst with Cowen & Co.
AlliedSignal posted first quarter earnings of $259 million or $0.92 a share on net sales of $3.3 billion, matching analysts' consensus expectations of $0.92 a share, according to First Call.

During the first quarter last year, the company earned $225 million or $0.80 a share on net sales of $3.8 billion. The 1996 first quarter included a light vehicle braking business which was sold in April 1996.
AlliedSignal also said it expects it will achieve 13 to 17 percent earnings growth in 1997 on eight percent sales growth.
AlliedSignal told analysts in a meeting that it expects it can hit the high end of that range, analysts said.

"They are saying they can hit the high side of 13 to 17 percent earnings growth for the year. They've done such a great job lately that it's hard to say that they are wrong, but it could be a bit of a struggle to get there," Shapiro said.
AlliedSignal said profit and sales growth will come from new products, plant capacity increases and improving conditions in several businesses.
The company said it expects its engineered materials unit to resume sales and earnings growth in the second quarter.
Sprague said he expects AlliedSignal will succeed in posting 17 percent earnings growth for year.
"The story is completely intact, and the company also has a tremendous amount of flexibility, particularly on the balance sheet. The company is sitting on almost $2 billion in cash," Sprague said.
